description: A country-by-country tour of Europe written for children by Wikijunior volunteers: what Europe and the European Union are, its mountains, peoples and languages, then a short profile of every European country with its history, land, people and sights. Each day you read one page together, color the country on your own map, and add a stamp to a homemade passport. It's a free, openly licensed book; every page is free to read on Wikibooks.
includes: Link to the free Wikibooks page for every lesson
A page for each of Europe's 50 countries, plus three that no longer exist
Map work every day on one blank map of Europe
Questions with answers for every lesson

lessons.title: Lesson 1: What Is Europe?
steps: Read the introduction together
Print or draw a blank map of Europe for the whole course
Talk about the difference between Europe and the European Union
questions: Which mountains mark the eastern edge of Europe?
Is Europe the same thing as the European Union?
answers: No; Europe is a continent, the EU is a group of countries

lessons.title: Lesson 2: The European Union

questions: How many countries are in the EU?

questions: What is a landlocked country?

answers: A country with no sea or ocean coast

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Languages of Europe
steps: Read the page together

questions: Which language is spoken by the most people in Europe?
Is Finnish an Indo-European language?
answers: No, it is a Uralic language

lessons.title: Lesson 6: The Fact File
steps: Read the explanation at the top and scan the table
Find the most crowded and the least crowded country
Start a 'country passport' booklet to stamp as you visit each country page
questions: What does 'population per km²' tell you about a country?
lessons.notes: Some figures in the table are older than the country pages; the country pages are more up to date.
